scope: KAI-6 verified municipality naming and Bitchu Matsuyama Castle metadata corrections

corrections.reason: Bitchu Matsuyama Castle is physically in Takahashi City (municipalityId Okayama:takahashi) and is a child of takahashi-city; it must not appear as a featured top sight of Okayama City.
Bitchu Matsuyama Castle is in Takahashi City, not Kurashiki; removed from the Kurashiki featured list (Korakuen retained as a same-prefecture regional pick).
Bitchu Matsuyama Castle is the canonical child of the Takahashi hub (same municipality Okayama:takahashi); featuring it restores the hub page top-sight section.
Featured list is a verbatim copy of the Matsuyama City (Ehime) record: both castles are in Ehime, ~700 km from Miyagi. Matsushima Bay is in Miyagi (parent sendai-city).
Nearby list is the Shikoku cluster copied from the Matsuyama City record; Shikoku cities are 500+ km from Miyagi with no modeled connection.
Nijo Castle (Kyoto) features Nikko shrines and Kegon Falls, both in Tochigi ~350 km away; batch-import error (Kanto cluster).
Nearby list is a Kanto cluster (Tokyo/Kanagawa/Chiba) on a Kyoto record; no modeled connection and geographically impossible as "nearby".
Mount Maya (Kobe) features Kochi Castle, ~250 km away in another prefecture; batch-import error. (nearbyDestinationIds kept: flagged as suspicious in the audit report, not corrected.)
Mount Hakodate features Ashigara and Jogashima, both in Kanagawa ~800 km away; batch-import error (Kanto cluster).
Nearby list is a Kanto cluster on a Hokkaido record; no modeled connection.
Related list is a verbatim copy of hakone-town's list (Gunma/Oita onsen towns); unrelated to Mount Hakodate.
Current officialWebsite URL returns 404; the official castle site (Takahashi City Tourism Association) is the canonical visitor page.
Official hours: 9:00-17:30 Apr-Sep (last entry 17:00), 9:00-16:30 Oct-Mar (last entry 16:00); closed Dec 29-Jan 3. Previous "Daily" claim was wrong (no winter closure, wrong close time).
Official hours with seasonal last admission and Dec 29-Jan 3 closure recorded with provenance.
Official Takahashi City page describes the site as a castle (現存天守12城, 天守の残る唯一の山城); kind=castle matches sibling castle records and drives scheduled opening-hours assessment.
Official Korakuen hours: 7:30-18:00 Mar 20-Sep 30 (entry until 17:45), 8:00-17:00 Oct 1-Mar 19 (entry until 16:45), plus summer evening openings. Previous "09:00-17:00 Daily" was wrong.
Seasonal last-admission times recorded with provenance.

Kurashiki is served by the Sanyo Shinkansen at Shin-Kurashiki Station (official JR West station page, JRおでかけネット, timetable shows Tokaido/Sanyo/Kyushu Shinkansen directions), but shinkansen was not authorized in transportOptions, so origin-aware matching (Tokyo-Okayama shinkansen corridor in ground-routes.json) returned no estimate and cards showed "N/A" travel time. transportOptions.shinkansen = 200 is a mode-authorization gate plus neutral-browsing reference value matching the sibling okayama-city convention; origin-aware durations always come from ground-routes.json, never from this value.
Okayama City is the municipality hub for Okayama Prefecture; its official Japanese municipality name is 岡山市.
Official English municipal usage for the Chofu City government portal is Chofu City; the repository city-hub convention requires the City suffix.
Keeps the localized English canonical-name copy consistent with the corrected root name.

corrections.oldValue: A fantastic trip to Boso Peninsula. Known for its road trip and ocean vibes, it offers a great escape with an overall score of 9.7.
corrections.newValue: Japan's only surviving mountain castle with its original keep.
corrections.reason: The previous note described a Boso Peninsula road trip and was a copy-paste contamination; the official castle site describes Bitchu Matsuyama as a surviving original-keep mountain castle.
